text:
karen_cs: heads-up — AcmeRetail (acct: acme_ret) just escalated. Their embeddings calls to our eu-west-1 endpoint are failing with dimension_mismatch and spotty latency (500ms->2s). They say it started ~1h ago after a client deploy. Error payload below.

eli: can you paste the exact error/req_id and a repro curl? also which model they call.

karen_cs: req_id=R-20260314-ACME-9988. Customer says they call `open-embedder-v1` via our sdk with default region. Sample error from their logs:
```
{"error":"dimension_mismatch","message":"Embedding dimension mismatch","expected":1536,"got":1024,"model":"open-embedder-v1","request_id":"R-20260314-ACME-9988"}
```

maria: quick note — we saw a small routing spillover around 17:02 UTC where eu-west dedicated pool hit 95% and router rerouted ~4% of traffic to hosted-eu, causing some cold-start traces. logs: `ROUTER: overflow -> hosted-eu1 (spinup gpu-37)`. Might be related.

eli: dimension mismatch + routing spillover is odd. dimension mismatch implies either client expects the wrong model dims or we returned vectors from a different model/quantization. karen, can you get the exact request payload (body headers), and whether the SDK specifies model alias or exact model revision? Also did the client pin model version or use `model: open-embedder-v1` (which we rotated yesterday to v2)?

karen_cs: customer used `model: open-embedder-v1` without pinning. Their deploy happened ~16:50 UTC. They gave this curl snippet:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-embedder-v1","input":["quick brown fox"]}'
```

sameer: ok flagged — we rolled `open-embedder-v1` to v2 yesterday which changed internal vector size from 1024->1536 (breaking change). We should've published a semver-major. If the customer still expects 1024 they'll get dimension_mismatch. But why are some calls returning 1024 and some 1536 (mixed)?

ops_sam: routing logs show a mix: requests hitting dedicated eu-west pool (which still has v1 pinned for some tenants via older instance image) returned 1024. Requests overflowed to hosted-eu (newer image with v2) returned 1536. Router trace example:
```
[17:01:54Z] ROUTER call=R-20260314-ACME-9988 route=dedicated-eu-west pool=p-eu-01 srv=embedder-v1
[17:02:01Z] ROUTER call=R-20260314-ACME-9991 route=hosted-eu1 pool=hosted-eu srv=embedder-v2 COLD_START=true
```

maria: that explains both errors and latency spikes (cold_start for hosted fallback adds ~700-1200ms). Also batching differences matter: dedicated pool had batching policy min_batch_size=8, hosted has min_batch_size=2. Some single-shot requests were waiting until batch fill, adding 150-300ms.

eli: so root causes: (1) model alias `open-embedder-v1` is ambiguous across deployments (some nodes have v1, some v2) — we did a partial rollout; (2) overflow routing spilled traffic to a pool with different model revision -> dimension mismatch; (3) cold starts + different batching policies caused latency variance.

karen_cs: immediate next steps I gave customer: a) pin exact model revision (e.g., `open-embedder@20260313-v1`), b) set `region=eu-west-1` in SDK/base_url so they don't route to hosted fallback, c) fall back to reindex vectors if they migrate to v2. Customer asked for a quick repro they can run to confirm.

eli: for repro and mitigation, ask customer to run two requests and compare dimension header:
```
# single request
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-embedder-v1","input":["test"]}' -i
# check X-Embedding-Dim header or response.error
```
If they see `X-Embedding-Dim: 1024` sometimes and `1536` other times, routing mix confirmed.

sameer: action items for eng-runtime: (1) enforce model alias consistency across pools during rollouts — do not serve different dims under same alias; (2) add server-side check to return descriptive error if alias maps to mismatched dims at router-level instead of letting it hit model and fail; (3) add rollout flag to prevent spilling incompatible variants. I'll open a PR for the alias pinning policy.

ops_sam: infra actions: (1) investigate autoscale thresholds for dedicated-eu pool, increase burst capacity threshold to avoid immediate spillover, (2) prewarm a small number of hosted instances for critical customers flagged as high-SLA to avoid cold starts, (3) audit batching configs across pools for parity. I'm creating infra ticket INF-2026-78.

karen_cs: CS actions: I sent the customer pinned model suggestion + repro steps. Asked for logs of `X-Region` header and `request_id`. Also offered to re-run a few calls from our side if they share a short-lived token.

maria: temporary workaround for customers: set `?routing=strict` on API calls to force same-pool routing (not recommended long-term). Also we can update SDK to warn when a pinned alias changes vector size.

eli: can we add an automated alert: when alias rollout changes vector dim, notify ops, runtime, and affected tenants?

sameer: yes. I'll prototype an alert hook that scans model metadata (dim) and flags alias-to-variant mismatches pre-rollout.

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-48210 linked to INF-2026-78 and ENG-RUNTIME-312. Assignee: sameer, ops_sam.

karen_cs: final — pls update this thread with status. I'll keep AcmeRetail in the loop and will request repro tokens. :pray:
